2. Sri Pradeep H.S. learned counsel for petitioners submitted that, petitioners are children of Tatappa @ Muninagappa and they are absolute owners of land bearing Survey no.52, measuring 22 guntas situated at Naganayakanahalli village, Channarayapatna Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural District.
It was further submitted that said property was joint family property and revenue documents standing in name of late Tatappa @ Muninagappa.

It was submitted that even O.S.no.679/2021 filed against petitioners for partition, had ended in rejection of plaint under Order VII Rule 11(a) and (d) of CPC, on 22.09.2023.
3.

It was further submitted respondents - authority had initiated acquisition proceedings for forming industrial area and issued Preliminary notification on 06.11.2014 and Final NC:
2023:KHC:40677 notification on 15.11.2018.

It was submitted that though petitioners were entitled for higher compensation under consent award, without offering opportunity to avail same, General Award was passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO), which was under challenge.
It was contended that under consent award, compensation was considerably higher than under General Award.

It was submitted that under similar circumstances, this Court allowed several writ petitions,
including W.P.No.31702/2018 disposed of on 29.11.2018..
Relying upon same, sought for granting similar relief.

4. On other hand, Sri Hanumantharaya Lagali, learned AGA for respondent no.1 and Sri P.V.
Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 and 3 submitted that respondent no.3 was constrained to pass General award as petitioners had merely filed objections, without relevant documents of title.

It was submitted that, if petitioner submits relevant documents, same would be considered for passing consent award under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Smt. Narasamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68014364/
3 Development Act, 1966.
5.

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Areas Smt. Narasamma vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
From above submission, it would appear that insofar as failure to provide opportunity to avail compensation under consent award, matter would stand covered under above referred decision.
As only reason assigned for not passing consent award is failure to produce documents to establish title, it would be appropriate to dispose of writ petition by issuing suitable directions.
Hence, I pass following:

ORDER Writ petition is allowed in part, impugned General Award bearing no.KIADB/LAQ-  2/1475/2022-23 dated 13.07.2022 at  Annexure-A passed by respondent no.3 is  hereby quashed insofar as it relates to  petitioners' property.
Petitioners to produce documents to establish title in respect of acquired land, within two weeks.

Thereafter respondent no.3 is directed to consider same for passing award and pay compensation in terms of Section 29 (2) of KIAD Act, 1966, within three months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

It is made clear that in event of dispute with regard to title, General Award at Annexure- 'A' which is quashed herein would revive.
NC: 2023:KHC:40677

Needless to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as a positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law.

Sd/-
